sections.h2: Who handles billing at the Onslow Tax Office
sections.html:
One office does the whole job: listing and valuing property, then sending and collecting bills. Its Collections Division covers the county plus Holly Ridge, Jacksonville, North Topsail Beach, Richlands and Swansboro, and it also takes vehicle tax on the sliver of Surf City inside Onslow.

Visit 234 NW Corridor Boulevard in Jacksonville any weekday; service runs from 8 until 5. Extensions: 910-989-2200 (Administration), 910-989-2201 (Listings), 910-989-2202 (Collections), 910-989-2204 (Land Records) and 910-455-7431 (Appraisal). Cash and checks work at the counter. Cards and e-checks go through the web payment portal, where a convenience charge applies.

Before you list, call Collections. A parcel may owe both a county charge and a municipal one, and Land Records handles boundary and owner name questions.

Onslow grew from 177,772 residents in 2010 to 204,576 in 2020, with an estimated 217,175 in 2025. There are 91,470 housing units and 75,265 households, 63.7 percent of them owning (2020 to 2024). Owned homes sit around $236,400 and rents around $1,265. Roughly one household in five moves in a given year, and 1,372 building permits went out in 2025.

With people moving in and out steadily, payoff and title questions come up often. Contact the tax office before you sign a contract.

Bills are mailed in July and are due September 1. A bill turns delinquent once January 5 passes without payment. Registered vehicles go through the state's tag and tax system.

Interest begins January 6 under G.S. 105-360: 2 percent through February 1, then 0.75 percent a month. Liens can be advertised from March through June under G.S. 105-369.

For 2026 the due date stayed at September 1, with delinquency after January 5, 2027, even though mailing ran later than usual.

The reappraisal dated January 1, 2026 was postponed a year, so this year's bills rest on the prior reappraisal's values. Session Law 2026-8 and Session Law 2026-47 allowed the delay, and new values arrive in 2027.

Onslow reappraises every four years under a 2001 resolution, starting January 1, 2006. State law allows counties to shorten its eight year maximum.

  • Your 2026 value should mostly match 2025, with changes only for construction or other alterations as of January 1, 2026.
  • Your bill can still rise, since the tax rate set by the Board of Commissioners and by any city or fire district also drives it.
  • An appeal already filed against the 2026 reappraisal value stays alive, and the outcome applies when that value takes effect in 2027.
  • December 31, 2026 is the final day to contest the value in use this year, the delayed reappraisal value, or both.

For the 2027 tax year, the usual appeal deadlines and steps return. For the current rate on your parcel, ask the Tax Office or read the rate in the county's adopted budget, since a rate is only final once the Board of Commissioners adopts it.

Ask for an informal review first. The formal route under the Machinery Act differs by property type.

A real estate review must be requested before the spring formal appeals begin. Yearly personal property and vehicles get 30 days from the bill date.

Appeal sequence for an Onslow County parcel
StageTiming
Informal reviewBefore spring formal appeals (real estate); 30 days from billing (personal property, vehicles)
County board hearingBoard's first session falls between early April and early May; request a hearing before adjournment
State commissionWritten notice within 30 days of the mailed board ruling

The statutes behind this are G.S. 105-322 and G.S. 105-290. Because of the delay, confirm current dates with the Tax Office.

The county's exemption page points to exclusion and deferment options, and the General Statutes define them. Only one of these three can apply to a household.

  • G.S. 105-277.1 applies to owners who are 65 or older or totally and permanently disabled and whose income stays within $38,800 for 2026. It excludes $25,000 or half the home's value, whichever is greater.
  • G.S. 105-277.1C excludes $45,000 for a disabled veteran, whatever the age or income.
  • G.S. 105-277.1B limits tax to 4 percent of income, or 5 percent for incomes above the limit up to $58,200, with the remainder deferred as a lien.

File Form AV-9 with the county assessor, ideally in January; the assessor takes it through June 1 before the tax year. The circuit breaker must be renewed annually. A sale triggers repayment of up to three years of deferred tax, so those owners should request the total before listing.

Active duty families can read the county's military page, which covers vehicles, boats and mobile homes. It asks for a current Leave and Earnings Statement at each tag renewal from anyone claiming a different home state.

sections.h2: Documents to collect before you sell
sections.html:
Closings move faster when tax documents are in hand. Gather these while the house is on the market.

  • The current bill for every taxing unit on the parcel, including any town that bills separately from the county.
  • A payoff from Collections with a good-through date, and a second one if closing might slip past a month end.
  • Any open appeal, since appeals filed against the delayed 2026 reappraisal value remain pending and will apply when that value takes effect in 2027.
  • Any AV-9 paperwork, if you receive an exclusion or circuit breaker benefit.
  • Land Records contact details for any boundary or owner name mismatch between the deed and the parcel record.

Commissioners adopted the FY2027 budget on June 29, and tax rates come out of that budget, so request the current rate for your parcel.

Unpaid tax sticks to the parcel from the listing date, together with interest and costs. If ignored, it can be advertised and foreclosed under G.S. 105-374 or 105-375, and Collections can tell you which route would apply.

Request a payoff that names each taxing unit and gives an expiry date, since interest changes on January 6 and after February 1. Add the seller's deed tax ($1 per $500 of price, paid to the register) and the recording fees in G.S. 161-10. A private cash sale lets you control price and timing and skips lender steps. If the house is empty, inherited or worn, Cash Home Buyers can quote an as-is price for comparison.

faqs.q: When do Onslow bills fall due?
faqs.a: September 1. Bills become delinquent when unpaid after January 5 of the next year, and interest begins on January 6 under G.S. 105-360.

faqs.q: Where is the Onslow Tax Office?
faqs.a: At 234 NW Corridor Boulevard in Jacksonville. It opens at 8 on weekdays and closes at 5. Call 910-989-2202 for Collections or 910-989-2200 for Administration.

faqs.q: Is the 2026 Onslow appeal window still open?
faqs.a: Yes, appeals can be filed through December 31, 2026, for the value in use this year, the delayed reappraisal value or both. The usual deadlines return for 2027, so call the Tax Office.

faqs.q: Which towns does the Onslow County Tax Office bill for?
faqs.a: The county, plus Holly Ridge, Jacksonville, North Topsail Beach, Richlands and Swansboro. Only vehicle tax is collected for the Onslow portion of Surf City.

faqs.q: Must a seller pay what is owed on the parcel?
faqs.a: Yes, until the balance is paid. Unpaid tax is a lien from the listing date. Ask Collections for a payoff and have the closing agent settle it at closing.
